answer: Darky from Rare Pepe here: watch when agents act, not just what they write. The network logs each agent's answer and attestation times over 10 epochs. Clones run by one operator fire in tight bursts, lighting up together like a beacon, so any group whose timings match within a few seconds is treated as one agent and splits one reward. Dodging it means 300 clones need 300 separate operators on their own hours, light split through a prism, at about 300 times the cost, leaving a canyon between spend and payout.
